function: Antenna-domain channel extrapolation from 8 selected antennas to all 64 (ASN plus AEN) and frequency-domain interpolation over 1200 OFDM subcarriers (DSIN) for channel estimation (p. 1, 4-5).
system: 64-antenna BS (semi-uniform rectangular USRP array), single-antenna users (four mobile antennas), TDD-like OFDM at 3.5 GHz, 20 MHz; no RIS (p. 3, 7, 10).
method: Supervised deep learning: antenna extrapolation network (FNN plus ODE-based fine stage), antenna selection network, and residual MLP (DSIN) for subcarriers; trained offline on measured pilots, run online (p. 4-5).
data_channel: Own OTA measurements, 64-antenna USRP prototype at 3.5 GHz, indoor office LOS and NLOS, static and 1 m/s users; over 1000 pilot symbols per location (p. 10-11).
test_conditions: Train on 8 measured antenna ports or 100 pilot subcarriers, test on the other 56 ports or 1100 subcarriers of the same data; pilots swept 25-100 (p. 11-13).
baselines: Non-learned: linear and SAGE extrapolation; zero-order hold, linear and cubic-spline interpolation; the prototype's own 64-antenna detection. Learned: none earlier; only uniform antenna selection, an ablation (p. 11-13).
metrics: NMSE of the predicted channels, EVM and detection SNR (dB) of uplink QPSK data (p. 11).
complexity: none; Table I gives layer widths only (p. 4) and the on-board inference speed is stated without a figure (p. 6).
openness: https://github.com/www09324063/64-MIMO-prototype-system, cited for prototype details and demo video; code or data release not stated (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 10: "In the OTA experiment, we tested various indoor locations". Training and validation both use the authors' own over-the-air measurements from the 64-antenna USRP prototype at 3.5 GHz (p. 1, 11).
q2_support: p. 11: "ports are used to validate the extrapolation results". Validation uses the remaining antenna ports and subcarriers of the same measurements (p. 11-12); the paper says the model must be retrained after a restart (p. 8); no cross-scene, cross-band or fine-tuning test is reported.
q3_support: p. 12: "zero-order holding, liner interpolation, and cubic spline interpolation algorithms". All comparisons are with non-learned methods (also linear and SAGE, p. 11); no earlier learned method, such as [26] whose network is adapted (p. 2), is compared, and uniform selection is an ablation of the ASN (p. 12).
q4_support: p. 6: "two neural networks to achieve the computational speed of". Qualitative only: no order of complexity, operations, parameter count or inference time is reported; Table I (p. 4) lists layer widths only.
q5_support: p. 10: "In the OTA experiment, we tested various indoor locations". The mark rests on training and testing with measured data; the GitHub link (p. 11, footnote 1) is cited only for prototype details and a video, without a stated code or data release.
notes: Included, area 2: DL channel extrapolation (JASEN) and interpolation (DSIN) on a 64-antenna OTA prototype, with measured NMSE, EVM and SNR (p. 11-13); the BS has 64 antennas (p. 3, Table III). q1 and q5 rest on the authors' own measured data; for q5 the reviewer should confirm that unreleased measured data count and whether the GitHub link (p. 11) is a release, since the paper does not say so. q2 is 0: the pilot-number sweep (p. 13) is probably separate training because the DSIN input is the pilot channel (p. 5), but this is not stated. Whole paper read, with Tables I and III and Figs. 13-27 opened as images.
